openings.claim: Does Z1 help through quantity reminders or through attention to transfer into envelopes? Its combined change leaves this dependency unresolved.
openings.delta: Keep exterior names and written quantities identical; vary marking immediately before versus immediately after transfer.
openings.prediction: If transfer attention matters, after-transfer marking reduces omissions between correctly counted picks and envelope contents.
openings.rival_prediction: Quantity confusion alone predicts similar omissions with identical quantity cues, regardless of marking order.
openings.defeat: Matched blocks show no transfer-stage advantage for after-transfer marking, while discrepancies arise entirely during picking.
openings.probe: Within the two-volunteer budget, alternate matched short blocks. The other volunteer audits counted picks and filled envelopes, records discrepancies and corrects them before closure. Include writing, audits and corrections in elapsed time. Keep materials on the existing table and stop by 90 minutes. This distinguishing probe does not establish 60-kit success.
assumptions: Exact pattern specifications and matched allocations are accessible.
The comparison and corrections fit the remaining time.

openings.claim: Does A1's local-batch advantage survive replenishment and checking costs across all 60 kits? O5 exposes a stock-access dependency absent from O4's short batch.
openings.delta: Evaluate total elapsed work, including preparation and opening reserve packets, rather than extrapolating filling pace.
openings.prediction: A durable local-batch advantage persists across replenishment episodes after preparation and audits are counted.
openings.rival_prediction: The apparent advantage reflects uninterrupted small-batch stock; replenishment and staging erase it despite fewer crossings.
openings.defeat: Local batches reduce crossings but total audited assembly exceeds 90 minutes or needs more than one distribution correction.
openings.probe: Use two volunteers and existing tally sheets to log preparation, filling, replenishment and correction times during the proposed full attempt. Measure table occupancy before opening packets; reject arrangements exceeding it. Stop at 90 minutes and report unfinished kits. Full intervention remains unproven.
assumptions: Reserve quantities suffice for the assigned pattern mixture.

critiques.issue: Its bundled probe cannot identify quantity guidance versus transfer attention; Q1 distinguishes these explanations.
Stopping early enough assumes an unestablished completion reserve; Q2 measures the whole budget and preserves failure visibility.
